gloss: a godsend; just what was needed at just the right moment

definitions.gloss: a godsend; a timely offer arriving exactly when needed
definitions.explanation: Literally "a boat when you need to cross." Describes help or an opportunity that turns up precisely when one is stuck, making an unwelcome problem easy to solve.

examples.japanese: その{誘|さそ}いは{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}だった。
{困|こま}っていたので、{彼|かれ}の{申|もう}し{出|で}は{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}だった。
examples.english: I was in trouble, so his offer came just at the right moment.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し{先|さき}を{探|さが}していたところに{社宅|しゃたく}の{話|はなし}が{来|き}て、まさに{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}だった。
examples.english: Just as I was hunting for a new place, the offer of company housing came up — a real godsend.

notes:
USAGE:
Usually predicative — {渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}だ / だった — and frequently reinforced with まさに (exactly, truly). It describes the timing of an offer, so there is normally someone or something providing the help.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- まさに{渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}: a godsend indeed
- {渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}と{引|ひ}き{受|う}ける: to accept, seizing the timely chance
- {渡|わた}りに{船|ふね}の{申|もう}し{出|で}: a perfectly timed offer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {棚|たな}からぼたもち: an unexpected windfall — pure luck with no effort or need involved
- {地獄|じごく}に{仏|ほとけ}: salvation in dire straits — stronger, for rescue from genuine desperation
